_comment: Model manifest for the provider model catalog (services/model_catalog.py).
For MOST providers this is a pure fallback: it is consulted ONLY when a live
/models probe fails (network down, credential unreachable inside the backend
container, provider 5xx), and every entry served that way is flagged
status=manifest_fallback in the API so the UI can say so out loud.
⚠️ GROK IS THE EXCEPTION AND IT IS DELIBERATE — DO NOT 'CLEAN THIS UP'.
For grok this file is MERGED INTO a successful probe (union, deduplicated;
see _MANIFEST_UNION_PROTOCOLS in model_catalog.py), because the Grok Build
CLI ships model slugs that NO HTTP surface reports. Measured 2026-07-28:
cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/models (with every client-surface header the
0.2.93 binary knows), `grok models` and ~/.grok/models_cache.json ALL return
exactly grok-4.5 — while composer-2.5-fast is present inside the binary next
to the bundled 'Cursor Composer toolset and prompt'. If the grok entry below
were deleted as 'stale handwork', that knowledge would be gone and no API
could give it back. It is manifest-driven ON PURPOSE.
cli_only: true marks a model the CLI knows but the wire protocol refuses.
Such entries are DISPLAYED (so the operator learns they exist) but are NOT
bindable — POST /models/catalog/bind rejects them with 422. Offering a model
that 400s on first use would be worse than not listing it at all.
This file is NOT a source of truth about what a runtime RUNS —
runtimes.model_identifier stays the only answer to that question.
Keyed by wire protocol (harness_compat.runtime_protocol), not by runtime slug:
anthropic/grok/kimi are single-endpoint protocols. The 'openai' protocol has
no entry on purpose — every openai runtime is a different endpoint (local vLLM,
LM Studio, Ollama Cloud, ...), so a shared static list would be a lie.
Note on kimi: since 2026-07-28 the kimi adapter reads the CLI's own config
(~/.mc/agents/<slug>/kimi-config/config.toml) token-independently, so the
kimi block below is a last-resort net only — it is normally never reached.
Verified live on 2026-07-28.

anthropic.note: api.anthropic.com/v1/models, verified 2026-07-25 (11 models). Fallback only — a live probe replaces this list entirely.

grok.note: MERGED INTO the live probe, not replaced by it (see _comment). cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/models — the Grok Build CLI proxy, NOT api.x.ai. The public xAI API advertises ~10 models; the CLI proxy exposes exactly one, and only that one is drivable by the grok harness over HTTP.

models.note: Im grok-Binary 0.2.93 enthalten (neben dem mitgelieferten 'Cursor Composer toolset and prompt'), aber von KEINER HTTP-Quelle gemeldet: /v1/models liefert unter jeder client-surface nur grok-4.5, ebenso `grok models` und models_cache.json. Direkt getestet am 2026-07-28 gegen cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/chat/completions mit den CLI-eigenen Headern: HTTP 400, 'Model not found: composer-2.5-fast' (grok-4.5 im selben Lauf: HTTP 200). Deshalb NICHT bindbar — hier nur dokumentiert, damit der Eintrag nicht als vergessene Handarbeit wieder verschwindet.

kimi.note: Letztes Netz. Primaerquelle ist seit 2026-07-28 die CLI-Config (~/.mc/agents/<slug>/kimi-config/config.toml, tokenunabhaengig) — dieselbe Datei, die `kimi provider list --json` liest. api.kimi.com/coding/v1/models liefert dieselben IDs, braucht aber einen Access-Token mit ~900 s Lebensdauer.
